metadata.title: Review quotations
metadata.description: Adversarially reviews the propositions and quotations in a document against the sources cited for them and against the wider law.

variants.label: Review quotations and support
variants.result: An adversarial critique of the document's propositions and quotations, each supported by the document and by external authority
variants.description: Verifies quotations against their cited sources, then adversarially vets every proposition the document advances against case law, legislation and journal sources, including later treatment of the decisions it relies on.
variants.skill_md:
# Review quotations and support

Adversarially review the selected document. Everything it asserts is in issue, not only its quotations. Work through these steps in order and do not answer until step 3 is done.

1. Verify the quotations. Call quote_check with document_id set to the document resource, and page through all results using offset. Where a citation is ambiguous, read and search the available sources, identify the intended source, and pass links as [{quoteId, occurrenceId}] back to quote_check using the returned quotation and citation candidate IDs. Compare exact wording, omissions, additions and punctuation. This step is the floor of the review, not its subject.

2. Read the document and list the propositions it advances — its statements of law and the inferences it draws from the evidence.

3. Research each proposition against the law itself, before writing anything. Use search_sources across case law, legislation and journal articles rather than relying on the document's own selection of authority, and read the passages you find. Note up the decisions the document leans on to find later treatment. Note up a decision even when its own text is not in the installed corpora: later decisions and journal articles that discuss it are themselves the evidence.

Test each proposition for authority that does not say what it is cited for, a holding stated without its qualifications, exceptions or dissent, reliance on a decision since distinguished, doubted or overtaken by statute, a rule stated at the wrong level of generality, an omitted contrary line of authority, and an inference the cited evidence does not carry.

Every finding rests on two retrieved passages: the passage in the document under review, and a passage from an external legal source — a case, statute or journal article — that establishes or contradicts the proposition. A finding supported only by the document under review is not a finding; drop it or go back to step 3 and find the authority.

Discuss the findings as a prose critique, the strongest objection first, identifying the document passage, the authority it relies on, the source passage that undercuts or qualifies it, and what the document would have to show instead. State unresolved sources and the limits of the review. Then offer to create a durable report or apply proposed edits, and follow an explicit request for either directly.

If the user requests an Excel workbook, call quote_check with export_workbook: true and analysis: [{quoteId, text}] carrying your findings. Keep mechanical evidence distinct from your legal assessment. For other requested report formats, use the available document and file tools.
